panicPatterns.title: System hang (watchdog)
panicPatterns.explanation: A core system process stopped responding for several minutes, so macOS restarted the kernel. The process is named after "no successful checkins from" in the report.
panicPatterns.advice: If it is WindowServer, suspect graphics: external displays, docks and adapters, screen recording or window-management apps. Unplug accessories and update or remove such apps.

panicPatterns.title: Sleep / wake failure
panicPatterns.explanation: The Mac failed to go to sleep or wake up in time.
panicPatterns.advice: Disconnect USB / Thunderbolt accessories and docks before sleeping, then retest. Apps that keep devices busy (backup, sync, VPN) can block sleep.

panicPatterns.title: Graphics processor (GPU)
panicPatterns.explanation: The panic was raised by the graphics driver.
panicPatterns.advice: Update macOS, then test without external displays and without GPU-heavy apps (games, 3D, video export). If it repeats on a clean system, contact Apple support.

panicPatterns.title: Internal storage (SSD controller)
panicPatterns.explanation: The panic involves the SSD controller.
panicPatterns.advice: Check free space (keep at least 10 %), back up now, and run First Aid in Disk Utility. Repeated storage panics on Apple Silicon need Apple support.

panicPatterns.title: Kernel memory exhausted
panicPatterns.explanation: The kernel ran out of memory for its own structures, usually because a kernel or system extension leaks memory.
panicPatterns.advice: Look at third-party kernel and system extensions (security, VPN, file systems) and update or remove them.

panicPatterns.title: USB / Thunderbolt accessory
panicPatterns.explanation: The panic involves the USB or Thunderbolt stack.
panicPatterns.advice: Test without docks, hubs and adapters, then reconnect them one at a time. Update the dock firmware if the vendor offers one.

panicPatterns.title: Invalid memory access in the kernel
panicPatterns.explanation: Kernel code read or ran from an invalid address. This is usually a bug in a kernel extension, more rarely a hardware fault.
panicPatterns.advice: If a non-Apple extension appears in the backtrace, update or uninstall it. Otherwise update macOS and watch for repeats.

panicPatterns.title: Overheating
panicPatterns.explanation: The panic mentions a thermal event.
panicPatterns.advice: Keep the vents clear, use the Mac on a hard surface and check which apps load the CPU or GPU in Activity Monitor.
